sentiment.reason_it: I mercati azionari e obbligazionari sono chiusi per il fine settimana. Il VIX è sceso a 16.70, mentre l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in positivo (+0.37%). Il DXY è salito dello 0.13%. Il petrolio è in aumento (+0.94%).

market_impact_summary.it: Mercati tradizionali chiusi. Il focus si sposta sulle crypto. Bitcoin in calo (-3.66%) a $74,499. Ethereum (-4.91%) a $2,022. Solana (-5.66%) a $81.96.
market_impact_summary.en: Traditional markets closed. Focus shifts to crypto. Bitcoin down (-3.66%) at $74,499. Ethereum down (-4.91%) at $2,022. Solana down (-5.66%) at $81.96.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.68%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.87%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei, se fossero aperti.

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 in rialzo dello 0.37%, VIX in calo dello 0.36%, DXY in rialzo dello 0.13%, oro in calo dello 0.41% a 4521 dollari l'oncia, petrolio in rialzo dello 0.94% a 103.54 dollari. I rendimenti: US 10Y Yield in calo dello 0.61% al 4.55%, BTP 10Y stabile a 3.73%.

Kevin Warsh ha giurato come nuovo presidente della Federal Reserve. La Banca d'Inghilterra potrebbe alzare i tassi solo in caso di carenze energetiche. L'UE punta su tassi fermi e più investimenti pubblici.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul comparto digitale, che opera 24 ore su 24 Bitcoin nella seduta precedente ha chiuso in calo dell'1.33% a 74,484 dollari. Il flusso netto degli ETF su Bitcoin è stato di -100.9 milioni di dollari, in declino.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
Bitcoin scende del 3,66%, portandosi a settantaquattromila quattrocentonovantanove dollari. 
I flussi degli ETF mostrano un deflusso di circa cento milioni di dollari, cento virgola nove milioni di dollari per la precisione. 
Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche di mercato e dalle aspettative sugli asset digitali.

Le altcoin mostrano perdite significative: Ethereum scende del 4,91% a duemilaventidue dollari, 
Solana perde il 5,66% a ottantuno virgola novantasei dollari e 
BNB scende del 3,40% a seicentotrentasei virgola trentasei dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a ventotto, in zona Fear, 
suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 
The Nikkei closed up 2.68%, Shanghai up 0.87%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets, if they were open. 
In the previous session, S&P 500 up 0.37%, VIX down 0.36%, DXY up 0.13%, gold down 0.41% to $4,521 per ounce, oil up 0.94% to $103.54 Yields: US 10Y Yield down 0.61% to 4.55%, BTP 10Y stable at 3.73%. 
Kevin Warsh has been sworn in as the new president of the Federal Reserve. The Bank of England may raise rates only in case of energy shortages. The EU is aiming for stable rates and more public investment. 
No relevant macroeconomic data out today. 
While global stock markets are observing the usual festive pause, the spotlight remains on the digital sector, which operates 24/7 Bitcoin in the previous session closed down 1.33% to $74,484 The net flow of Bitcoin ETFs was -$100.9 million, in decline. 
Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... 
Bitcoin is down 3.66%, bringing it to $74,499 
ETF flows show an outflow of around $100 million, precisely $100.9 million. 
This movement could be influenced by recent market dynamics and expectations on digital assets. 
Altcoins show significant losses: Ethereum down 4.91% to $2,022, 
Solana loses 5.66% to $81.96 and 
BNB down 3.4% to $636.36 
The Fear & Greed Index is at 28, in Fear zone, 
suggests caution among investors. 
We are waiting for economic data out today. To delve deeper into today's themes, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Confusion over UK sanctions on Russia undermines a Western response that was already too slow and half-hearted
articles.snippet: Confusion over UK sanctions on Russia undermines a Western response that was already too slow and half-hearted Expert comment sfarrell.drupa… 22 May 2026 In trying to limit the pain on itself, the West has pulled its punches in hurting Russia. Nearly four and a half years after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the West has still not found the knock-out punch which derails the Russian economy. Numerous Western sanctions packages – twenty now from the EU – have not decisively turned the course of the war. Part of the problem is that Russian President Vladimir Putin likely long planned this war and built up buffers accordingly – probably as far back as the first imposition of Western sanctions on Russia following the annexation of Crimea in April 2014. articles.title: NATO Must Die
articles.snippet: Some claim that the threats Europe is facing, especially after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, can create the momentum toward political union that the euro crisis and then the pandemic failed to generate. Right or wrong, one thing is clear: a functional defense union requires political union, and NATO's existence is inimical to it.

articles.title: The Cultural Component of National Security
articles.snippet: Since Russia’s full-scale invasion four years ago, Ukraine has become the world’s most consequential defense laboratory, trialing innovations that can strengthen European resilience. But the country has also demonstrated that national security depends as much on cultural identity as on military strength.

articles.title: Inside Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovation Loop
articles.snippet: This exclusive Cogs of War interview is with Catarina Buchatskiy, the co-founder and director of analytics at the Snake Island Institute, a Kyiv-based defense analytics center, and Viktoriia Honcharuk, the institute’s director of defense technologies. We asked them to share their views on how Ukraine’s military and defense firms turn battlefield feedback into rapid innovation, what Western investors and defense tech companies can learn from Ukraine, and what a future Ukraine-West defense industrial partnership might look like. articles.title: The Kid Rock Flyby Controversy and the Erosion of Military Professionalism
articles.snippet: During Congressional testimony from Department of Defense leadership last week, Representative George Whitesides asked Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, “How does canceling a command-initiated review support a culture of accountability?” But before the secretary could answer, Whitesides instead decided to direct the question to the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. Dan Caine. articles.snippet: Global oil markets remain under severe stress as Hormuz disruptions, weak economic data, and tightening inventories reshape energy flows worldwide. With Europe posting its worst macroeconomic numbers since 2023 and the IEA warning of oil markets hitting the ‘red zone’ by July-August, ICE Brent is unlikely to fall…

articles.title: EU Warns Energy Prices Will Stay Elevated Through 2027
articles.snippet: Top EU officials said Friday that oil and gas prices are expected to remain elevated through at least the end of 2027, with the fallout from the Iran war likely to keep pressure on inflation and economic growth. Speaking after a meeting of eurozone finance ministers in Cyprus on Friday, EU Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said higher energy costs are now expected to drive inflation to 3.1% this year and 2.4% in 2027—well above the bloc’s earlier forecast of 1.9% for this year. The concern is no longer just fuel prices themselves.…
